findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared against replay event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body: `gen_request_data` interleaves errors with breadcrumbs by checking `error_events[idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. The error timestamp comes from the nodestore event payload, which is epoch seconds. The `event["timestamp"]` from an rrweb replay segment is normally epoch milliseconds. With real data every error then compares as 'earlier' than the first replay event, so all errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of in chronological order. The Seer summary receives a wrong timeline. The tests use the same unit for both sides (`now.timestamp()` for both, and small numbers in `test_get_request_data`), so they cannot catch this. Normalise the units, for example by multiplying the error timestamp by 1000, and add a test that uses millisecond replay timestamps.

findings.title: Per-issue get_recommended_event() lookup when building PR comments
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue in the comment (up to 5). That performs an event lookup (Snuba plus nodestore) per issue, synchronously in the comment-building path, just to show an environment name. Failures are swallowed and logged only at `info`, so persistent lookup problems will go unnoticed and the comment silently loses the environment. Consider a single batched lookup, or reading the environment from data already available on the group or query.

findings.title: Issue title placed unescaped inside markdown link text and truncated mid-token
findings.body: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` puts the raw (user-controlled) issue title inside `[**{title}**]({url})`. A title containing `]`, `[`, `**` or `](...)` breaks the link or lets the title alter the rendered link in the PR comment. `_truncate_title` cuts at 50 characters without regard to markdown, so it can also leave an unbalanced `**` or bracket and mangle the rest of the comment. The title should be escaped, or have markdown-significant characters stripped, before it is interpolated.

findings.title: Unknown report types reject the whole batch with 422
findings.body: `type` is a `ChoiceField` limited to 8 values, and a single invalid report makes the endpoint return 422 for the entire array. The Reporting API can deliver other report types to a collector (e.g. `network-error` or newer types), and browsers batch reports. One report of an unlisted type discards all valid reports in the same request. The previous code only used the types as hints and accepted everything. For a data-collection endpoint it is safer to skip or tag unknown types than to fail the batch.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness and is not enforced when both are missing
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` use `self.initial_data.get(...)` truthiness, so a value of `0` (valid for both `age` and `timestamp`) is treated as absent. A report with `age: 0` and `timestamp: 5` therefore passes. Field-level validators also only run when the field is present, so a report containing neither `age` nor `timestamp` is accepted, although the comments say exactly one spec format is required. Use `is not None` / `in initial_data` checks and add an object-level `validate()` requiring exactly one of the two.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty columns and data
findings.body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag is on, every table widget renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`. The real `result.data` / `result.meta`, field aliases, loading state and custom field renderers are all ignored. Any org with the flag enabled sees every dashboard table widget as an empty table. If this is intentional scaffolding, it should be marked clearly. Otherwise pass `result.data`/`result.meta` (converted to `TabularData`) and the columns.

findings.title: Default autofix automation tuning silently changed from 'low' to 'off'
findings.body: `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` and the `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` project option default both change from `"low"` to `"off"`. Every project that never set the option explicitly changes behaviour on deploy: autofix automation turns off, and the API/serializer now reports `off`. This has nothing to do with the PR title (replay bulk delete), and the PR description is just 'Test 5'. It should be a separate, clearly described change, with a decision on whether existing projects need a migration to preserve their effective setting.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check. Requests from orgs without the feature (which get a 404) are still counted as assemble API usage, which skews the metric. Also, `request.user.id` is None for org-auth-token requests, so those events carry no user. Move the call after the feature check unless counting rejected requests is intended.

findings.title: New max_segment_id=None handling is not actually exercised
findings.body: The test now feeds `max_segment_id: None`, but it patches `delete_matched_rows`, so the real `_make_recording_filenames` / `delete_replay_recordings` code that gained the `None` early-return is never run. A regression back to `range(None + 1)` would still pass. Add a direct unit test of `_make_recording_filenames` with a `None` segment id, or an unmocked `delete_matched_rows` test.

findings.title: 60s processing deadline for a batch of up to 100 external identity refreshes
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` loops over up to `chunk_size=100` auth identities. Each `check_single_auth_identity` makes a network call to the SSO provider's `refresh_identity`. A fixed `processing_deadline_duration=60` allows only about 0.6s per identity, so a slow provider can hit the deadline. `check_auth` has already bumped `last_synced` for the whole chunk, so the identities that were not reached will not be re-selected until the next interval (about a day). The final `check_auth.apply_async` reschedule is also skipped. Size the deadline to the chunk, or reduce the chunk size.

findings.title: Query key omits organization; isLoading/attributes semantics changed
findings.body: The react-query key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, but `queryOptions` contains no organization slug, and the fetch URL does depend on `organization.slug`. Cached attribute keys can be reused across organizations within a session. The hook also now returns `isLoading: isFetching`, which is true on every background refetch rather than only the initial load. `attributes` can now be `undefined` (it was previously always a `TagCollection`). Callers that gate UI on `isLoading` or assume a defined object may flicker or break. The old `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false` options were also dropped.

findings.title: Saved queries with multi-yAxis visualizes will always look modified
findings.body: A Visualize now holds a single yAxis. A saved query stored in the old format `{yAxes: [a, b]}` is parsed into two Visualizes, which `toJSON()` serialises as `[{yAxes:[a]},{yAxes:[b]}]`. `valueIsEqual(visualizes.map(v => v.toJSON()), singleQuery?.visualize, true)` then never matches the stored value. The Save button is permanently highlighted as 'has changes', and the saved overlay is split into separate charts. There is no migration or normalisation of the stored `visualize` shape on load.
